correctness.rationale: Identity B_n²=(C_{2n}-1)/16, C_n²=(C_{2n}+1)/2, c_n²=(C_{2n-1}-1)/2 and exact geometric window sums prove three formulas (1). The order-two unimodular step recurrence for C_{2n+j} yields D_j=16 for even j and 96 for odd j, reducing each infinite gcd to (3). 2-adic congruences for B_k and C_j settle parity factors, while modulo-three recurrence plus triple-angle identity settle the exceptional factor three; primes ≥5 reduce to gcd(k,B_k). Reconstructed edge cases k=1,2,3,6 and tested all k=1..240 using exact arithmetic and all 7620 assertions from the actual accompanying verify.py. Finite testing is not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2023 source explicitly asks for formulas for these squared-window gcds, recording only experimental ratios (Sec. 6.1, Question 30). The new contribution is an exact unified arithmetic identification of three families with gcd(k,B_k) and full proof of the local factors, not the previously observed ratios. The 2022 generalized-Fibonacci-square theorem uses G(n+2)=G(n+1)+G(n), not the balancing characteristic t^2-6t+1. published-finding corpus, literature and OEIS comparisons gave no matching all-k formula. Novelty remains conditional on the inspected public corpus; unindexed equivalences are a risk.

value.rationale: This is a unified exact response to three of four natural square-window sequence families raised in a named published Question 30, not an arbitrary congruence slice. The identification with gcd(k,B_k) proves the observed ratios, fixes the 2-/3-adic boundary factors uniformly for all k, and yields the new common property that every resulting square-window gcd divides the window length. Although the remaining term-index gcd is not simplified to a residue-only expression, the three infinite invariants are determined exactly.
